candidates.name: Brown tumor of hyperparathyroidism
support_spans: Histopathology of finger tumor
Numerous giant cells with multiple osteoclastlike nuclei and giant multinucleated cells dispersed in contact with fibers associated with small vessels
candidates.why: The presence of a large tumor on the distal part of the right fourth finger with histopathological features of fibrous tissue, woven bone, and giant cells is consistent with a brown tumor, a rare complication of hyperparathyroidism.
candidates.protected_reason: This diagnosis may be easily missed due to its rarity and the fact that it can be mistaken for other bone lesions.

candidates.name: Osteitis fibrosa cystica
support_spans: Radiography showed complete lysis of the underlying phalanx and periosteal bone resorption in the phalangeal tuft band
Skull radiography showed pattern of trabecular resorption with 'salt-and-pepper' appearance
candidates.why: The radiographic findings of bone resorption and the 'salt-and-pepper' appearance of the skull are consistent with osteitis fibrosa cystica, a condition associated with hyperparathyroidism.
candidates.protected_reason: This diagnosis may be overlooked due to its nonspecific symptoms and the fact that it can be mistaken for other bone disorders.
